messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Example 4
Hospital course: An 81-year-old woman was brought in after a fall at home. She could not weight-bear and the right leg was shortened and externally rotated. A pelvic radiograph showed a displaced subcapital fracture of the right femoral neck. She underwent hemiarthroplasty on day one.
Answer: S72

Example 5
Hospital course: A 19-year-old man presented with 18 hours of periumbilical pain that migrated to the right iliac fossa, with anorexia and a low-grade fever. There was guarding at McBurney's point and the white cell count was 15.2. Laparoscopy confirmed an inflamed, non-perforated appendix.
Answer: K35

Example 6
Hospital course: A 64-year-old woman with a history of oestrogen-receptor-positive breast carcinoma treated five years earlier presented with progressive thoracic back pain. Magnetic resonance imaging showed deposits in T7 and T9 with no cord compression. Biopsy confirmed deposits of breast origin and she received palliative radiotherapy to the spine.
Answer: C79

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: N/A
Age: 24
Gender: Female
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted to our hospital with acute pulmonary edema due to severe aortic valve insufficiency. She had previously been diagnosed with Takayasu's disease and had undergone multiple surgeries, including replacement of the distal ascending aorta and hemiarch, stenosis of celiac artery and superior mesenteric artery, and stenosis of the orifices of both renal arteries. She had a graft used to direct blood flow from the right internal iliac artery to all stenosed arteries. She also underwent a right nephrectomy due to acute thrombosis of the right renal artery graft. The patient was on steroid treatment since the diagnosis of her disease.

Treatment:
The patient underwent surgery to address the aortic valve insufficiency. The procedure was performed through a median sternotomy, and a composite graft with a mechanical valve was implanted. The patient's postoperative course was uneventful, and she was discharged from the hospital on the 10th postoperative day.

Follow-up:
The patient had a one year clinical follow-up that showed normal echocardiographical results, and she was doing well in normal daily activities.

Pathology:
Part of the dilated aortic root wall was sent for histological examination, which verified the diagnosis of Takayasu's arteritis.

Note:
The patient's condition was complex and required surgery to address the aortic valve insufficiency. The patient's postoperative course was uneventful, and she had a good one year clinical follow-up.

Answer with the three-character category only.

text:
The principal diagnosis is the condition chiefly responsible for the admission. She was admitted with acute pulmonary edema from severe aortic valve insufficiency, and the surgery addressed that insufficiency. The aortic insufficiency is due to Takayasu arteritis, which is coded M31.4 (aortic arch syndrome).

ICD-10-AM has an etiology/manifestation convention. Aortic valve insufficiency in a systemic disease could be coded I39 (endocarditis and heart valve disorders in diseases classified elsewhere), but that is a manifestation code and cannot be sequenced first. The underlying condition would be sequenced first, which gives M31 as the principal diagnosis.

Alternatively, I35 (nonrheumatic aortic valve disorders) could be argued. However, I35 has an exclusion for conditions of unspecified cause, and here the cause is known. The pathology confirmed Takayasu arteritis, and the aortic root was dilated because of the arteritis. M31 is therefore the most defensible choice.

**M31**
